question: A customer support system receives billing questions, technical bugs, and account cancellations. Each category needs a differently tuned prompt, and an initial step must first determine which category a given ticket belongs to before further processing. Which pattern should the team implement?
options: A) Orchestrator-workers, where a central LLM decides at runtime which subtasks the ticket requires and assigns them to worker LLMs
B) Prompt chaining, where each ticket is chained through billing, then technical, then cancellation prompts in sequence
C) Parallelization, running the billing, technical, and cancellation prompts simultaneously and merging whichever completes first
D) Routing, where an initial LLM call classifies the ticket and directs it to the specialized prompt for that category
correct_answers: D) Routing, where an initial LLM call classifies the ticket and directs it to the specialized prompt for that category
explanations: Incorrect. Orchestrator-workers is for tasks whose subtasks are unpredictable and must be dynamically decomposed, not for a single classification-to-specialized-prompt decision.
Incorrect. Prompt chaining passes every ticket through every step in sequence; here only one category-specific prompt should run per ticket, not all three.
Incorrect. Parallelization runs independent subtasks or repeated attempts concurrently; it does not classify an input into one of several distinct categories.
Correct. An initial classification step that directs the ticket to a category-specific specialized prompt is the defining shape of routing.
